# R349 — Precision of recurrent-model activations and scratch

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Source and public-evidence review only. The Main GPU measurement is active; this review did not inspect or touch it. No local tests, imports, AST tooling, builds, model/GPU/profiler work, process/service access, Git operations, receipt edits, cleanup, or hash scans were performed. This report is the only new artifact.

## Finding

The useful distinction is where rounding happens. Public Gated Delta Net (GDN) implementations commonly accept ordinary BF16 activations while keeping the recurrent accumulator/state in FP32 and writing the layer output in the activation dtype. That is a credible design pattern for reducing the size of intermediate tensors without making each recurrent state update low precision. It is not evidence that Strata's particular scratch tensors can be rounded without quality loss: every rounded q/k/v, gate, or beta value still changes the inputs to the recurrence, and that error can influence all later tokens.

A newly found merged vLLM change is a concrete warning against indiscriminate narrowing of a transient scalar. In a 1,000-step GDN recurrence, rounding sigmoid(beta) to BF16 and widening it back on each step caused much larger state/output error and degraded a serving task set. The fix preserved the sigmoid result in FP32 while still using BF16 model activations. This argues for selective precision by operation and data lifetime; it does not establish that recurrent state should always be FP32 or that all activation scratch must be FP32.

## Evidence that separates activation and state dtypes

- The [Flash Linear Attention fused recurrent GDN implementation](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention/blob/main/fla/ops/gated_delta_rule/fused_recurrent.py) keeps recurrent accumulation in FP32, emits the ordinary output in the value tensor's dtype, and allocates the final recurrent state as FP32 by default. This is direct implementation evidence of distinct activation/output and state dtypes. It is not a precision comparison or a quality guarantee for another model.
- The [vLLM fused GDN state-dtype dispatch](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py) and Qwen GDN implementation expose FP32 and BF16 recurrent-state paths. Availability is implementation support, not a quality result. The [SGLang JAX KV-cache documentation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-jax/blob/main/docs/architecture/07-kv-cache.md) likewise describes FP32 as the recurrent-state default and BF16 as an option, with convolution state treated separately. This records engineering choices, not validation at Strata's target context length.
- The strongest newly located error study is the merged [vLLM PR #53877](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53877). Its H100 test uses BF16 activations and runs 1,000 recurrent steps. The bug applied a BF16 round-trip to sigmoid(beta) at each step; the fix stopped that round-trip. With FP32 state, reported relative L2 error moved from 1.085934e-4 to 5.308258e-9 for state and from 2.464718e-3 to 1.809305e-5 for output. With BF16 state, it moved from 2.139224e-4 to 1.091964e-5 for state and from 3.226935e-3 to 1.919026e-4 for output. The PR also reports strict-loop cases falling from 20/42 to 1/42 and answer closure rising from 8/42 to 39/42. These figures compare the beta-rounding bug with the fix; they do not compare BF16 state against FP32 state. They show that keeping a sensitive per-step coefficient in FP32 can matter even when activations and, in one test condition, stored state are BF16.
- A corroborating [SGLang issue #38975](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38975) reports a local 1,000-step test with FP32 recurrent state and BF16 activations: state relative L2 changed from 1.41e-3 to 1.05e-7 after the same beta-rounding correction. The report author explicitly did not claim whole-model quality validation, so the merged vLLM PR remains the clearer evidence source.
- Precision can also drift in the opposite direction. In [vLLM issue #51779](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51779), an author reports Qwen3.5-397B differences when a BF16 Q/K normalization path was promoted to FP32 and cast back instead of following the model's BF16 operation semantics. Reported per-layer Q/K relative L2 was about 0.27%, recurrent-core relative L2 about 2.2951%, and a single-token cached-decode NLL difference was 0.09991 nat/token across a 60-layer TP8 run. The issue says a patched rerun was still needed to attribute the NLL difference, and this is Qwen3.5 rather than Strata's Qwen3.8 target. It is therefore a caution about reference operation dtype, not proof that lower-precision scratch is safe.

The source and measurements support a narrow conclusion: low-precision activation tensors with FP32 recurrent arithmetic are a real design used in GDN serving; the exact dtype at each nonlinearity still matters, and framework support alone does not establish model quality.

## Strata source mapping and candidate boundary

The current source reviewed was the qualified-copy worktree at commit `410904c9` (`diag-native-copy-queue-qualified-20261013`). In `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, the GDN scratch structure holds FP32 `qkv`, `z`, `ab`, `gate`, `beta`, `hbuf`, and `y`, alongside a 16-bit `y_h` output. The `gdn_set_bytes(T)` accounting includes the FP32 planes and `y_h`; `gdn_floats` includes the recurrent matrix and convolution history. GDN state is passed as `float*`. In `src/prefill/kernels.cpp`, `gdn_recurrence` uses FP32 state and local arithmetic, writes the FP32 `y` plane and also writes 16-bit `y16`; the downstream native projection consumes `y_h`. The FP32 `y` plane appeared only in allocation and the recurrence call in the reviewed call path, so removing its materialization while retaining FP32 local arithmetic and the existing low-precision output is the lowest-risk capacity candidate, subject to preserving any diagnostics or other build configurations that consume it.

The other activation planes are higher risk. `qkv`/`hbuf`, `z`, `gate`, and `beta` cross a kernel boundary and feed recurrent or output calculations. Storing a reduced-precision copy there could lower scratch bytes, but a cast changes every consumed value; a token-by-token recurrence can carry that perturbation forward even while its state remains FP32. A disciplined experiment would cast only at the producer/consumer boundary to the checkpoint's intended activation dtype, widen at the FP32 recurrence consumer, and protect sigmoid(beta) and sensitive reductions unless direct measurements show otherwise.

The MoE planes `GU` and `Dm` are also FP32 in the reviewed prefill allocator. `GU` feeds a nonlinear gate/up operation; `Dm` holds expert contributions before routing/combination. They are separate candidates rather than one blanket conversion: first test reduced storage after the FP32 projection and before the SwiGLU consumer for `GU`, then test `Dm` with FP32 widening and accumulation. The latter still discards per-expert contribution bits before summation. Prior source-eligibility findings are recorded in R251; this report adds no runtime or performance claim for either path.

Persistent recurrent-state narrowing is a different and riskier proposal than narrowing a one-use scratch plane: it rounds the state after repeated updates. The reviewed Strata recurrence keeps that state FP32. Public support for BF16 state and the vLLM beta fix do not establish quality at 256K context or for this quantized model. No direct public paired-quality result found in this pass validates reduced Strata GDN state or scratch at that length.

## Decision and validation needed

Treat “FP16/BF16 activation scratch + FP32 recurrence/state” as a plausible design to evaluate, not an accepted Strata optimization. First pursue eliminating the apparently unused FP32 `y` store if diagnostics and all consumers confirm it. For actual reduced-precision inputs, evaluate each plane independently and preserve operation dtype semantics. Keep recurrent state FP32 until a paired, full-target-context study measures the accumulated effect.

A useful local comparison would hold model, prompts, sampler and software constant and compare baseline against one changed plane at a time. Record next-token log-probability/KL and top-1 changes, answer/task correctness, and retrieval/code behavior, with results binned by position and including the target 256K length; include repeated runs and a predeclared acceptance threshold. This review did not run or authorize that experiment. Prior reports R289/R299 already cover the earlier Qwen FP8 residual, direct recurrent-state quantization papers, and the need for local paired validation; they are not repeated here.
